children: U.S. crude contracts turned lower by midday Wednesday after the International Energy Agency said its member countries would complete oil stock releases as soon as possible as part of their previous commitment to address supply disruptions due to the Middle East conflicts.
At 11:55 a.m. ET, November NYMEX West Texas Intermediate crude futures were down around 45cts to $89/bbl, and December WTI was 25cts lower at $88.20/bbl.
Prior to the IEA statement, WTI was up more than $1/bbl.
London-based December ICE Brent was up about 35cts to $100.90/bbl and January Brent was 55cts higher to $98.15/bbl.

Refined product futures also weakened but remained higher. November NYMEX ULSD was up 10.25cts to $4.6715/gal and December ULSD was 9.7cts higher at $4.52/gal. November RBOB was up 1.05ct to $3.2835/gal and December RBOB was 2.25cts higher at $3.1105/gal.
IEA also said in the statement the full release of all stocks that had been pledged but have not yet been released would bring about 100 million bbl of crude oil to the market.
In addition, the agency said its member nations support the prioritization of diesel releases from their reserves, and IEA stands ready to release those stocks to the market if needed.
